This paper introduces a real-time dynamic N-1 screening framework that addresses this gap by estimating, for each counterfactual single-phase transmission fault, the probability of transient overcurrent on critical grid elements. The output is an operator-facing dashboard that ranks (a) faulted lines whose outages most frequently lead to dangerous transformer overloads, and (b) transformers that consistently overload across top-risk scenarios, both of which are actionable indicators for real-time situational awareness. The approach models post-fault electromechanical dynamics using a linear stochastic formulation of the swing equations with short-lived, fault-localized uncertainty, and combines analytic transient evaluation with cross-entropy based importance sampling to efficiently estimate rare but high-impact events. All N-1 contingencies are evaluated in parallel with linear computational complexity. The framework is demonstrated on the IEEE 118-bus system, where it reveals latent high-risk lines and transformers that remain invisible under deterministic dynamic or static N-1 analysis. Results show orders-of-magnitude computational speedup relative to brute-force Monte Carlo, enabling practical deployment within real-time operational cycles.

papers.title: eIRWR: Enhanced Iterative Random Walk with Restart for Scalable Root Cause Analysis in Microservices
papers.summary: Root cause analysis (RCA) in microservice systems must find the faulty service behind symptoms that spread across hundreds or thousands of dependent services. Graph-based random walk methods propagate anomaly evidence over the service dependency graph. However, existing anomaly-restart walks restart from the raw anomaly vector, which is often dominated by strongly anomalous downstream victims rather than the less anomalous source. Through a controlled ablation of a basic anomaly-restart walk, the Iterative Random Walk with Restart (IRWR), we show that its ``resilience damping'' is equivalent to a higher restart probability in Personalized PageRank (PPR). Basic IRWR is therefore no stronger than a restart-tuned PPR, which we adopt as a fairer baseline. We then present Enhanced IRWR (eIRWR), which goes beyond restart tuning. It (a)~concentrates restart mass on the most suspicious nodes through power-law sharpening and (b)~adds self-loops and backward edges so that probability accumulates at cascade sources. On three large topologies (12K--25K nodes) from the Alibaba Microservice Trace Dataset, eIRWR is the most accurate of the compared graph-based methods at every level of root-cause visibility. At visibility $v = 0.3$, it reaches a Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) of $0.78$, about four times a restart-tuned PPR and nine times the best other baseline. At high visibility, it reaches MRR\,$= 0.95$ and runs in under 30\,ms on graphs with 17K nodes, so it is suitable for online use.

papers.title: Quantale-Enriched Co-Design: Toward a Framework for Quantitative Heterogeneous System Design
papers.summary: Monotone co-design enables compositional engineering design by modeling components as feasibility relations between required resources and provided functionalities. However, its boolean formulation cannot natively represent quantitative criteria such as cost, confidence, or implementation choice. In practice, these considerations are introduced through ad-hoc scalarization or by augmenting the resource space, which obscures system structure and increases computational complexity. Therefore, we develop a quantale-enriched theory of co-design in which resources and functionalities are quantale-enriched categories and design problems are quantale-enriched profunctors, which lifts co-design from boolean feasibility to quantitative evaluation. Series, parallel, and feedback composition remain valid over any commutative quantale, and change-of-base maps between quantales yield heterogeneous composition, so that subsystems evaluated in different local semantics can be composed in a common framework. Numerical examples on a target-tracking system and a UAV delivery problem demonstrate this framework and show how it avoids the drawbacks of boolean-only formulations.

papers.title: Consensus-based Economic Dispatch for Self-organized Local Energy Communities
papers.summary: The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) is transforming traditional distribution networks into dynamic, decentralized systems, creating a pressing need for scalable, autonomous coordination mechanisms that do not rely on centralized control or full system observability. papers.title: A Theory of Information Architecture for Networked Decisions: Freshness, Locality, and Coordination

papers.title: Fundamental Tradeoffs in Sampling, Transmission and Information Freshness: Instantaneous Feedback
papers.summary: We study a time-slotted generate-at-will status-update system over an erasure channel with transmission success probability $q$, subject to average sampling- and transmission-rate constraints $f_s$ and $f_r$, respectively. papers.title: A Lifted Hessian-Riemannian Gradient Flow for LQR Synthesis under Passivity Constraints

papers.title: Contingency Planning for Safety-Critical Autonomous Vehicles: A Review and Perspectives

We write the DeePC solution as an implicit ReLU network whose weights are built from Hankel matrices and whose activation patterns are the critical regions of the underlying quadratic program. This gives, directly from the Hankel matrices, the feasible set of DeePC as a polyhedral projection, its explicit piecewise-affine control law, and an exact linear model of the history window. We compute three invariant sets of histories: the maximal positively invariant set of the unsaturated linear branch, the region of recursive feasibility of DeePC without terminal ingredients, and the maximal control invariant set of admissible histories. We show these sets are nested and provide numerical examples.

papers.title: Hydrogen-Diesel Dual-Fuel Engine Operation Using Real-Time GRU-Based Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
papers.summary: Hydrogen-diesel dual-fuel (H2DF) combustion can reduce combustion-out CO2 emissions but exhibits nonlinear cycle-to-cycle dynamics at high hydrogen energy shares (HES), while the NOx-particulate matter (PM) trade-off must still be managed. The mean engine-out PM concentration is about 60% lower, while the mean engine-out NOx concentration increases by 105.1% without exhaust-gas recirculation. The controller tolerates feedback noise and model-plant mismatch from engine-speed variation, and it executes in 3 to 7 ms per engine cycle on low-cost embedded hardware within a modular rapid-prototyping toolchain. papers.title: Boundary Collisions and Weak Excitation in LQR Policy-Gradient Flows
papers.summary: Closed-loop stability concerns all initial states, whereas an LQR cost evaluates only the directions excited by a prescribed initial-state distribution. We study how this distinction affects Euclidean policy-gradient flows. For every nonzero deficient covariance rank, we construct relatively open families of controllable data and open sets of stabilizing initial gains whose exact gradient trajectories reach the stability boundary in finite optimization time. The state Gramian can remain positive definite at every time before collision. By separating the cost contribution of a critical mode, we obtain a local collision criterion based on direction attraction and motion toward the stability boundary. Adding excitation of strength $\varepsilon$ yields matching $Θ(\sqrt\varepsilon)$ bounds on the local minimum stability margin for trajectories that would otherwise collide. For a class of single-input, corank-one systems, these bounds hold over the entire trajectory without a common compact-set assumption. Numerical examples further illustrate the dynamics and scaling laws.

papers.title: The Grid's Own Language: A Common Information Model Layer for LLM Grid Assistants
papers.summary: Assistants built on large language models (LLMs) are entering power system operation. papers.title: Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling
papers.summary: Day-ahead load forecasts set balancing reserves, including the energy a pumped-storage plant holds against forecast errors. Both depend on three effects that are usually modeled separately, namely the thermal inertia of buildings, which makes load lag temperature, structural breaks, which shift demand, and the long memory of forecast errors, which keeps them from cancelling out. We prove that averaging building responses over Cole-Cole distributed time constants yields a fractional temperature kernel with nonnegative weights exactly when its order is at most one. A Bayesian information criterion that ignores long memory selects spurious breaks with probability tending to one, so breaks and memory are estimated jointly, and an online break detector keeps its false-alarm rate below any prescribed level. Long memory also makes the required storage energy grow faster than the square root of the horizon, so a second-order cone program schedules reserves from the joint distribution of hourly errors. On New England and Mid-Atlantic data including the 2020 pandemic, the proposed framework improves on the best of ten benchmarks by 15.7% and 10.3% in mean absolute percentage error. Its reserves breach the storage energy limit on 4.1% and 8.5% of days, against 36.7% and 57.5% with error correlations ignored.

papers.title: Sparse Stabilization of Continuous-Time Linear Dynamical Systems
papers.summary: Efficient use of communication resources is crucial for stabilizing a networked control system. Employing \emph{sparse inputs} and event-triggered control are efficient ways to utilize communication resources in networked control systems. This work considers the problem of stabilizing a continuous-time linear dynamical system (LDS) using $s$-sparse inputs. For this purpose, we consider \emph{switched} linear feedback control, where we construct a finite number of feedback matrices with at most $s$ nonzero rows. Using switched systems theory, we show that there exists an $s$-sparse input for any sparsity level $s \geq 1$ that ensures stability when the continuous-time LDS is stabilizable. In addition, using our approach, we can compute the required feedback matrices with minimal overhead even if the sparsity budget $s$ varies over time. We also minimize the maximum Frobenius norm of the feedback matrices, yielding sparse inputs with reduced control energy. We show that an upper bound on the control energy required for stabilization using an $s$-sparse input is inversely proportional to $s^2$, while maintaining the same exponential stability rate. Finally, we combine the design of the \emph{sparse inputs} with the event-trigger rule to further reduce communication resource consumption. Our sparse and event-triggered control strategy ensures that any stabilizable continuous-time LDS can be stabilized using $s$-sparse inputs under both state feedback and output feedback, for any $s\geq 1$. We illustrate our theoretical results for the task of stabilizing a mass-spring system.

papers.title: Distance-Certified Polyak-type Stepsizes for Subgradient Methods under Hölder Growth
papers.summary: In this paper, we consider nonsmooth convex optimization under a H{ö}lder growth condition, with quadratic growth and weak sharp minima as two important special cases. Existing subgradient methods often employ predetermined decaying stepsize schedules, whereas the classical Polyak stepsize selects its stepsize adaptively but requires knowledge of the optimal value. We introduce a new distance-certified subgradient method (\DCSG) that follows a one-step optimization principle analogous to that underlying the Polyak stepsize, without requiring the optimal value. Specifically, \DCSG{} maintains a valid upper certificate for the current squared distance to the solution set. The method selects each stepsize by minimizing the worst-case upper bound on the next squared distance over all distances consistent with this certificate. We show that the resulting minimax problem admits a closed-form solution, yielding an explicit adaptive stepsize update. Under uniformly bounded subgradients, \DCSG{} improves upon the convergence rate of the classical subgradient method and matches the state-of-the-art rates for Lipschitz convex optimization under H{ö}lder growth. In particular, it achieves linear convergence under sharp growth. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of \DCSG.

papers.title: Topology-Transferable Detection of Deep-Learning False Data Injection Attacks Through Residual-Energy Separation

papers.title: Low-Voltage Ride-Through in AI Data Centers via Coordinated Battery and Computing Load Control
papers.summary: The ability of large AI data centers to ride through grid voltage sags is critical to power system stability and reliability. This paper frames data center low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) as a DC-link power balance problem. Once the rectifier reaches its current limit, the power drawn from the grid decreases in proportion to the grid voltage. The DC-link capacitor can supply the resulting power deficit only briefly before the DC-link voltage falls low enough to trigger undervoltage protection tripping. To address this issue, this paper proposes effective control strategies for coordinating uninterruptible power supply (UPS) battery and computing load curtailment to offset the power deficit and enable LVRT at minimum control cost. Three control scenarios are studied: UPS battery support alone, computing load curtailment alone, and the coordinated use of both resources. Electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations using the TAMU-ERCOT AI data center model demonstrate that battery support and the coordinated strategy achieve LVRT for all tested sags, including a near-zero-voltage fault, while load curtailment alone rides through moderate voltage sags.

papers.title: A Re-Keying Game for Encrypted Multi-Agent Control under Persistent Threats
papers.summary: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) lets a coordinator control a fleet on encrypted states, but CKKS, the approximate scheme for real-valued arithmetic, returns noisy decryptions from which an adversary can recover the secret key. papers.title: Latent resonances in oscillator networks

papers.title: Robust Control Design for LTI Systems with Sampling-Time Jitter

papers.title: Control-Gibbs Distribution: Sampling for Optimal Control and Diverse Actions

papers.title: Velocity-Free Funnel Control of Euler-Lagrange Systems: An Artificial-Delay Approach

papers.title: From Grid to Chip: Power Architecture, Stability, and Flexibility of AI Data Centers
papers.summary: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) computing is transforming data centers into large, dynamic electrical loads. Their deployment is primarily constrained by energy availability and grid-connection capacity, which is further aggravated by the ability of power-delivery architectures, control systems, and computing workloads to operate reliably during fast grid disturbances. papers.title: Quantifying the Cost of Restoring AC Feasibility for Approximate Optimal Power Flow Solutions
papers.summary: Power system operations rely on approximate solutions of the AC optimal power flow problem, most notably the DC optimal power flow used in security-constrained unit commitment and economic dispatch, while convex relaxations, machine learning surrogates, and other approximations are studied extensively in the academic literature. The cost of this adjustment is not adequately understood. We apply it to the DC optimal power flow, the second-order cone and quadratic convex relaxations, and the AC optimal power flow solved to a loose relative tolerance of $10^{-4}$ instead of $10^{-8}$. Relative to the AC optimal power flow solution obtained from a local nonlinear optimization solver, and even with the minimum adjustment, the DC optimal power flow requires adjusting, on average, generators that account for 15.6% of total generation capacity and incurs a 1.10% cost increase; the convex relaxations require more adjustment (17.2% and 16.9%) but smaller cost increases (0.68% and 0.78%); and the loose-tolerance AC optimal power flow requires 6.1% and incurs 0.42%. These results indicate significant value in operating markets directly on the AC optimal power flow, which avoids the distortion of the dispatch and prices caused by heuristic feasibility restoration.

papers.title: A Nested Heterogeneous Multiscale Framework for Power System Dynamic Simulation
papers.summary: Power system dynamics involve multiple timescales, from electromagnetic transients of the network and inverter-based resources to electromechanical oscillations of synchronous generators and quasi-steady-state evolution of the operating point. Simulating these dynamics with a detailed electromagnetic transient model is computationally prohibitive, whereas existing methods reduce the model to focus on a single timescale and lose accuracy when dynamics of different timescales interact. This paper proposes a nested heterogeneous multiscale framework for highly efficient multi-timescale simulation of a power system represented by one unified detailed model. Rather than varying only the integration step, the framework adaptively shifts the simulation resolution among three nested levels so that the dynamics of interest at each stage are always captured, with the slower dynamics estimated on the fly from short detailed simulations at controlled accuracy. Theoretical analysis proves the stability of long steps during quasi-steady-state evolution and quantifies the attainable speedup. On a modified IEEE 39-bus system with frequency regulation and load restoration, the framework accurately reproduces the dynamics of all timescales and runs 15 to 18 times faster than conventional simulation of the detailed model. The accuracy and speedup of the proposed method are further verified on a 390-bus system, demonstrating its scalability to large power systems.

papers.title: Low-Data OOD Prediction of SAW Resonators with Simulation-Compensated Transfer Learning
papers.summary: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators are foundational to modern radio-frequency (RF) front-end architectures. However, models trained on limited fabricated devices generalize poorly to unmeasured design regions because of process-induced variations, while finite-element method (FEM) simulations, although inexpensive, exhibit systematic offsets from measurements. To predict device performance before physical prototyping, this work presents a simulation-compensated transfer-learning framework that uses computationally efficient 2.5-D FEM simulations as physics-based anchors and learns their calibration to the measurement domain. Using 4,236 measured lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) SAW resonators and 816 unique simulated configurations, five transfer strategies are systematically benchmarked under seven out-of-distribution (OOD) protocols spanning frequency, geometry, and material shifts. The proposed framework reduces OOD prediction error by 83.54% on average (up to 97.57%) relative to the Measurement-only baseline, with the best strategy selected per case, and raises the pooled R2 of frequency prediction to 1.000, offering an economically scalable route toward physics-guided, fabrication-aware machine learning for microelectromechanical-system (MEMS) acoustic-device design.

papers.title: Backstepping-Forwarding Design for Hyperbolic PIDE-ODE Systems with Distributed Interconnection and an Arbitrarily Large Input Delay
papers.summary: This paper studies first-order hyperbolic partial integro-differential equation (PIDE) and ordinary differential equation (ODE) cascades with distributed interconnection and an arbitrarily large known constant input delay. Within the backstepping--forwarding framework, a forwarding-type transformation is designed to reduce the distributed interconnection to an equivalent boundary-coupled Dirichlet cascade without requiring the PIDE to be open-loop stable. A subsequent backstepping design stabilizes the PIDE and the ODE while compensating for the input delay. Incompatible boundary conditions in the delay-compensation kernel equations may produce discontinuities along characteristic lines. We determine their jump locations and amplitudes and prove that the interface terms cancel when deriving the target equations, so the kernel discontinuities do not change the target system. Closed-loop exponential stability is established without additional plant restrictions to ensure kernel continuity. A numerical example illustrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Quantifying the power grid hosting capacity gained by coordinating distributed solar, battery storage and electrified flexible loads
papers.summary: Distribution grid hosting capacity is usually assessed with static, single-resource methods that treat distributed energy resources as fixed injections, which can understate how much solar generation and electrified load feeders can accept. We quantify the hosting capacity gained when solar photovoltaics (PV), battery storage, heat pumps and electric vehicles (EVs) are dispatched by network-aware coordination at 5-minute resolution, versus static operation of the same devices. On the IEEE 123-node feeder, we use a deterministic iterative method, a two-stage stochastic program that optimizes siting, and a Monte Carlo extension over 100 scenarios. With storage, heat pumps and EVs at 5%, coordination raises PV hosting capacity from 48% to 83% of peak load; with 10% storage, 20% PV and 5% EVs, heat pump hosting capacity rises from 9% to 55% of homes. When siting is co-optimized, PV hosting capacity rises from 24% to 98%, and the jointly feasible PV, heat pump and storage region grows about 22-fold. Coordination turns storage and heat pumps from substitutes into complements: with storage up to 100% of peak load, the feeder hosts PV up to about 200% of peak load and heat pumps in 90% of homes. Midday limits are relieved by storage charging and heat pump pre-cooling, evening limits by inverter reactive support, battery discharging and heat pump setback. Under input uncertainty, coordination raises mean PV hosting capacity by 64%; the absolute spread widens while the relative spread narrows slightly. At published reinforcement costs, the added capacity is worth roughly $0.6--1.5 million per feeder in deferred upgrades.

papers.title: Exact Output Steering with Vanishing Controls in Weighted Shift Dynamics
papers.summary: Exploiting the rich dynamics of wrapped weighted shifts and their residualizations, we characterize exact projected steering with vanishing initial controls. For wrapped shifts, steering is characterized by an expansive cycle multiplier and a residue separating the source and control channels. For structured machine-learning representations built from orbit dictionaries, we derive a two-scale gain condition for steering coefficients while preserving decoded outputs.

papers.title: Strategically Robust Linear Quadratic Dynamic Games
papers.summary: We study linear quadratic dynamic games where players are uncertain about each other's control policies or goals and consequently seek to be strategically robust. Building on recent work on strategically robust and risk-averse game theory, we first formalize the problem of strategically robust linear quadratic dynamic games. We show that these can be rewritten as simple transformations of linear quadratic games in which each player chooses a controller in a fictitious game in which they are faced with an adversary who is penalized for deviating from the other players' policies. This formulation naturally induces a novel notion of dynamic equilibrium, which we call a strategically robust dynamic equilibrium. We establish existence and uniqueness (in the subgame-perfect sense) of such equilibria and show that the equilibrium policies are Markovian, linear, and can be efficiently computed via coupled backward Riccati equations. Through numerical simulations, including experiments in a network game, we illustrate the benefits of strategic robustness in designing robust and resilient decentralized control schemes. Our experiments also expose a "free-lunch" phenomenon in games in which robustness does not incur a corresponding loss in performance but can yield improvements in players' utilities and social welfare.

papers.title: Metropolis Random Walks Escape Deep Basins Faster in Higher Dimensions
papers.summary: Simulated Annealing (SA) is a widely used stochastic optimization algorithm. It is of great interest to understand how its ability to escape local minima at a fixed temperature depends on geometry and dimension. In prior work, we derived closed-form expressions for the expected basin escape time of a constant-temperature SA process on a one-dimensional piecewise-linear landscape. In this paper, we extend the analysis to $D$-dimensional cubic basins defined by the infinity-norm energy $V(x)=\|x\|_\infty$. The walk proposes nearest-neighbor moves uniformly and escapes upon first reaching the outer shell, that is, any site with $\|x\|_\infty=N$. We construct a one-dimensional birth-death shell-quotient chain by collapsing each concentric shell in the Metropolis electrical network to a single node while retaining its total stationary mass. We derive a closed-form expression for the mean escape time $Q_D(N)$ of this shell-quotient chain as a function of the acceptance probability $p$, the basin depth $N$, and the dimension $D$. For fixed $D$ and fixed $0<p<1$, the quotient escape time scales as $Θ(α^N/N^{D-1})$ as $N\to\infty$, where $α=1/p$. Relative to $D=1$, this gives an asymptotic speedup of order $N^{D-1}$ within this family of cubic basins. We prove that the true Metropolis mean escape time $H_D(N)$, without shell averaging, has the same $Θ(α^N/N^{D-1})$ scaling, establishing a lower bound via Rayleigh monotonicity and a matching upper bound through an explicit low-energy flow construction using Thomson's principle. Numerical solutions that exploit the walk's symmetries quantify the discrepancy between the quotient and true-chain means for $D=1,2,3$.

papers.title: TDMOpt: LLM-Driven Cross-layer Dispatch for Transmission-Distribution-Microgrid Systems
papers.summary: Coordinating transmission networks, distribution networks, and microgrids enables distributed flexibility to support renewable energy integration and low-carbon operation. However, heterogeneous resources, cross-layer coupling, and varying operating requirements complicate the selection of models and coordination schemes that are both physically adequate and computationally tractable. A layered component library provides executable network, resource, objective, constraint, and coordination models. papers.title: On Fast Attitude Filtering Using Matrix Fisher Distributions with Stability Guarantee as an Observer
papers.summary: This paper addresses two interrelated problems of the nonlinear filtering mechanism and fast attitude filtering with the matrix Fisher distribution (MFD) on the special orthogonal group. By analyzing the distribution evolution along Bayes' rule, we reveal two essential properties that enhance the performance of Bayesian attitude filters with MFDs, particularly in challenging conditions. Benefiting from the new understanding of the filtering mechanism associated with MFDs, two closed-form filters with MFDs are then proposed. These filters avoid the burdensome computations in previous MFD-based filters by introducing linearized error systems with right-invariant errors but retaining the two advantageous properties. The proposed filter with right-invariant error is shown to be almost globally asymptotically stable for any trajectory on $SO(3)$ as a deterministic observer, leveraging its Wahba-type update and right-invariant construction. Moreover, we further prove the local exponential stability of the filter for single-axis rotations to reveal the effect of the two properties on the convergence rate. These stability results support the performance of the proposed filter with large initial error from a theoretical viewpoint, which to our knowledge, is not achieved by existing directional statistics-based filters. Numerical simulations demonstrate that proposed filters are as accurate as recent MFD-based Bayesian filters in challenging circumstances but consume far less computation time (by up to about two orders of magnitude compared with previous MFD-based attitude filters).

papers.title: Beyond Yes or No: Grading Observability of Power System Dynamic States with Symbolic Coefficients
papers.summary: Graph-based observability analysis runs in seconds where Lie-derivative tests take hours, but it answers only one question: is the system observable or not. It cannot say how well a given set of measurements supports state reconstruction. This paper extends the graph-based approach with symbolic observability coefficients computed from a symbolic Jacobian of the state-space equations, in which every dependency is classified as constant, nonlinear polynomial, or rational. We show that the coefficient tracks the analytical observability determinant of the Lie-derivative approach: it is zero when the determinant vanishes, lies strictly between zero and one when the determinant depends on the state, and equals one when the determinant is a nonzero constant. We apply the method to a seven-state synchronous machine and to the 21-state Western System Coordinating Council nine-bus system under several synchrophasor measurement configurations. On the nine-bus system, the coefficient grows from 0.0952 with one PMU to 0.1905 with two and 0.2857 with three, and the whole analysis runs in under five seconds. Configurations with the same number of PMUs receive the same coefficient, yet an unscented Kalman filter estimates the states with different accuracy for each. The symbolic coefficient therefore grades measurement sets beyond identifying root strongly connected components, while telling PMU locations apart still requires the numerical parameters of the system.

papers.title: Benign Geometry and Distributional Robustness of $\mathcal{H}_2$ Synthesis
papers.summary: In this paper, we study standard and distributionally robust $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis problem of a stabilizing state-feedback controller for discrete-time linear time-invariant systems. Without requiring a nonsingular disturbance controllability Gramian or a positive-definite control penalty, we establish that stationarity of a stabilizing gain in standard $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis is equivalent to global optimality and derive an exact Pythagorean identity for the performance difference. We then generalize the $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis problem by considering i.i.d. disturbances with zero mean and uniformly bounded second moments, and extend the stationarity-optimality equivalence to the corresponding distributionally robust $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis. Moreover, we show that every standard $\mathcal{H}_2$-optimal gain is simultaneously optimal for every such distributionally robust problem. Finally, we specialize the framework to Frobenius, Kullback--Leibler, and Wasserstein-2 ambiguity sets and obtain explicit characterizations of their worst-case covariances, which, in turn, provide performance certificates for a common optimal controller.

papers.title: Human-on-the-Loop Distributed Control of Grid-Interactive Buildings for Demand Response Participation
papers.summary: This paper proposes a human-on-the-loop distributed consensus control approach for demand-side management across multiple buildings. Specifically, a novel framework is introduced in which a human acts as the non-autonomous leader in consensus control of cooperative buildings participating in demand response programs. In this system, the facility manager in the facility building serves as the leader, determining the participation level of cooperative buildings in demand response events while simultaneously considering occupants' comfort. Cooperative buildings align their responses with the facility management building, despite lacking direct access to the facility manager's decisions, and this raises two coupled challenges: The manager's actions act as an unknown input to the leader, and the consensus protocol requires a state that cannot be measured. Because the input is unknown, the necessary observer should be an unknown-input observer to guarantee the performance, and the observer-matching condition required by conventional linear designs does not hold for this system. A human-on-the-loop leader-follower consensus protocol is introduced to manage energy use and balance thermal comfort, together with a nonlinear unknown-input sliding-mode observer that reconstructs the local consensus error in finite time without requiring the mentioned condition. Under exact measurements, continuous-time dynamics, and an admissible initial state, a componentwise certificate guarantees bounded tracking and bounds on ramp rate, comfort, and power when the leader power and the ambient temperature remain within prescribed limits. Simulation results validate the approach, demonstrating its ability to achieve consensus, maintain system performance, and enhance the adaptability of power grid operations under various demand response scenarios.

papers.title: Learning of LPV Models With Linear Fractional Representations: Initialization, Optimization, and Conditioning
papers.summary: Linear Parameter-Varying (LPV) models with Linear Fractional Representation (LFR) can describe a wide class of nonlinear systems with a control-friendly structure. However, identifying these models together with their scheduling map from input-output data requires solving a non-convex optimization problem that is highly sensitive to initialization. Consequently, existing methods often rely on many random initializations. Instead, our work proposes an initialization strategy based on the Best Linear Approximator (BLA). Furthermore, motivated by an analysis of the impact of rational-dependency LPV-LFR models on the conditioning of the non-convex cost, two multiple shooting methods that improve the conditioning, unconstrained multiple shooting (UMS) and encoder-based multiple shooting (EBMS), are compared. The initialization and multiple shooting methods are evaluated on a nonlinear mass-spring-damper example, showing that BLA initialization consistently yields accurate results, whereas random initialization has a large spread. The results also show that both UMS and EBMS reduce the spread for randomly initialized models. UMS is simple to tune and well suited to few sub-records, whereas EBMS can exploit many short sub-records to further improve conditioning, at the cost of training an encoder and tuning additional hyperparameters.

papers.title: Adversarial Observability and Performance Trade-offs in Optimal Control
papers.summary: We develop a feedback controller that minimizes the observability of a set of adversarial sensors of a linear system, while adhering to strict closed-loop performance constraints. papers.title: BEVCast: Path-Adaptive BEV for Efficient End-to-End Autonomous Driving

papers.title: SAFER: Navigating the Exploration-Exploitation Dilemma in World-Model-Based Planning for Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: An autonomous vehicle must foresee the consequences of its actions, especially in the rare, time-critical situations where crashes happen. A world model offers this foresight, but only within the coverage of its training data, which poses an exploration-exploitation dilemma. Within this coverage a planner can hardly improve on the data, and beyond it the model's errors mislead it. Logs of competent driving rarely contain the failures that would widen the coverage, and agents that learn from interaction gain them only by failing themselves, without being shown what to do instead. We propose SAFER, a framework that learns offline from failures that others make, judged by an expert, and keeps learning online from its own driving. Offline, partially trained agents and scripted, recoverable perturbations Stage failures in simulation, and an expert Annotates every visited state with its action and value, so that much of what the planner explores is covered before it drives. In planning, a chunked latent world model Foresees the consequences fast enough for real-time use, and a risk-aware sampling-based planner Evaluates candidate maneuvers by their return minus a bounded collision penalty. Online, a loop continuously Refines the model wherever this driving leaves the coverage of the offline data. In closed-loop evaluation against the compared methods, SAFER reaches the highest route completion and reward per step on the CARLA Leaderboard routes, 0.95 and 0.77 from a privileged bird's-eye view, and the highest episode reward in MetaDrive, 53.4 in regular and 49.0 in safety-critical traffic. papers.title: VoxSAOR: Semantic-Aware Occupancy Robustification via Aleatoric Uncertainty Modeling
papers.summary: Vision-based 3D occupancy prediction provides a dense semantic representation of scenes for autonomous driving and embodied perception, yet remains vulnerable to occlusion, depth ambiguity, and projection errors that induce spatially varying reliability in voxel features. At inference, proxy modeling and sampling are disabled, and all heads process the same observed features; their output probabilities are then averaged to produce a deterministic consensus prediction without requiring sampling. Experiments across multiple datasets and occupancy backbones demonstrate the effectiveness of VoxSAOR in improving semantic occupancy prediction, long-tail recognition, and predictive calibration. To enable expressive autoregression on continuous coordinates, we propose next-token diffusion, whereby a causal transformer denoises each token while attending to the clean tokens before it, without increasing context size. We train Nahual on a curated set of twelve 3D chemistry tasks ranging from microsolvation to molecular conformer search to adsorption on metal surfaces, with associated evaluation metrics and baselines. The result is a single set of end-to-end-trained weights that simultaneously performs all tasks and surpasses state-of-the-art models specialized for crystal structure prediction and property-conditional molecule generation. Our results demonstrate the viability of scaling generalist decoder-only models for native multimodal understanding and generation across language and chemistry. Code is available at https://github.com/the-matter-lab/nahual.

papers.title: Evaluating Video LLMs' Understanding of Corner Cases in Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: Natural language explanations promised by modern Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) offer autonomous driving systems a path toward detailed scene description and interpretable decision making on the road. While recent benchmarks have begun assessing these models on driving scenes, they mainly target routine traffic conditions and general comprehension tasks based on existing driving datasets and therefore fail to evaluate model performance on the rarest and most safety-critical driving events, also known as "corner cases". To provide a comprehensive evaluation of Video LLMs on precisely these scenarios, we introduce DashBench, a benchmark testing 25 Video LLMs on 1,709 carefully curated driving videos spanning not only collision-related corner cases but also rare non-collision ones. Through extensive prompts and open-ended question answering, we expose a critical capability gap: all evaluated models perform substantially below the threshold required for safety-critical driving applications, frequently misjudging or missing dangerous events on the road ahead and hallucinating non-existent agents or actions in their explanations. We believe DashBench, combining an extensive dataset with a rigorous evaluation toolkit and a detailed diagnosis of current model limitations, drives progress toward safer, more explainable autonomous driving systems. The code and data will be shared at: cornercase-dashbench.github.io

papers.title: Instant NuRec: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Reconstruction for Driving Scene Simulation
papers.summary: 3D simulation platforms are critical for autonomous driving because they enable end-to-end policy evaluation, thereby reducing development costs and improving safety. In recent years, neural simulation has become predominant, with methods such as NuRec playing a central role; however, these methods remain relatively slow and typically require per-scene tuning. In this work, we present Instant NuRec, a feed-forward neural reconstruction model that turns a short multi-view driving log into a fully simulatable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) world in a single forward pass. The model accepts multi-view input from a calibrated camera rig and emits a layered output consisting of static and dynamic 3DGS layers, a sky cubemap, and per-camera ISP corrections, while providing native support for non-pinhole camera models via 3DGUT. It reconstructs a 10-20-second multi-camera scene in roughly 1.5 seconds and achieves a PSNR on the Waymo Open Dataset that is 2.01 dB above the strongest evaluated baseline. Instant NuRec is deeply integrated into NuRec and is compatible with AlpaSim for closed-loop simulation.

papers.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
papers.summary: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch. Experiments covered colonoscopy, breast ultrasound and dermoscopy, with testing on held-out data from the training source and on independent datasets from other institutions. The adapted foundation model generalised better on every external dataset. Within the training distribution, the task-specific models remained competitive when training data were abundant, and delineated boundaries more precisely, while the foundation model more often missed small lesions. Only a small fraction of the foundation model required adaptation, and the capacity needed was determined by the imaging domain rather than by the adaptation method. A widely used polyp test set was also found to duplicate images from another benchmark. Foundation-model adaptation is therefore warranted where models must work across sites, with capacity selected on the target domain.

papers.title: Classical structural priors improve neural molecular representations in molecule language models
papers.summary: Classical molecular similarity is central to chemical information systems, yet molecule-language models trained on paired structure-text data do not necessarily organize molecular embeddings according to graded structural relationships. Here we introduce Structure-Aware Guided Alignment (SAGA), a training-only regularizer that uses Centered Kernel Alignment to align neural molecular representations with fingerprint-based Tanimoto similarity, without adding parameters or requiring fingerprints at inference. In MolCA and Atomas, SAGA improves molecule-text retrieval, shifts non-exact retrieval toward closer structural analogues, and increases average scaffold-split property-prediction performance, while molecular description and text-to-molecule generation are improved or preserved in single-run ablations. These results show that established chemoinformatics priors can make molecule-language representations more chemically faithful while retaining their multimodal utility.

papers.title: Structure-Guided Multi-Granularity Spatiotemporal Transformer for Efficient Monocular 3D Human Pose Estimation
papers.summary: Existing multi-granularity methods for monocular 3D human pose estimation emphasize spatial joint features while underusing skeletal structure, including global connectivity and temporal continuity. Moreover, modeling entire frame sequences incurs high computational costs. We propose a Structure-Aware Multi-Granularity Spatiotemporal Transformer that integrates structural priors across spatial and temporal representations for accurate and efficient pose estimation. A three-level feature extractor captures human topology at the joint, bone, and limb levels. Gated Adaptive Spatial Attention (GASA) embeds structural constraints into spatial attention, while Multi-Granularity Feature Enhancement (MGFE) uses hierarchical pooling and fusion to strengthen local details and global semantics. Temporal Segment Fusion (TSF) aligns temporal contexts across granularities to capture both short- and long-range motion patterns. Hierarchical Cross-Attention (HCA) promotes spatiotemporal interaction between granularities, and Keyframe Attention (KFA) selects informative motion segments to reduce redundancy and computational cost. Experiments demonstrate improved accuracy and efficiency over conventional Transformer-based approaches, highlighting the effectiveness of structure-aware multi-granularity modeling for monocular 3D human pose estimation.

papers.title: Large Language Model-based Optimization for Wireless Communication: A Survey
papers.summary: The growing complexity and dynamism of modern wireless communication frameworks have made real-time optimization essential for efficient resource allocation. Traditional optimization and machine-learning techniques often struggle with generalization, adaptability, stability, and scalability in heterogeneous, time-varying environments. Large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as powerful tools capable of reasoning over structured prompts and generating context-aware decisions in real time without domain-specific retraining. This survey provides a comprehensive review of LLM-driven optimization techniques applied to wireless communication problems such as power control, bandwidth allocation, task offloading, and intelligent surface configuration. We introduce a functional taxonomy of LLM-enabled wireless resource management strategies and analyze the prompt engineering methodologies employed in recent literature. Furthermore, we develop a generalized analytical framework that categorizes LLM-based optimization architectures, including direct solution generation, closed-loop optimization with external verifiers, and representation encoding within trainable neural pipelines. To demonstrate practical applicability, we present representative case studies on LLM-assisted beam prediction for millimeter-wave systems and adaptive wireless resource allocation. Finally, we discuss emerging hybrid AI approaches for wireless networks.

papers.title: A Simulation Framework with Guaranteed Error Bounds for Safety and Fuel-Efficiency Analysis of Vehicle Platoons
papers.summary: Vehicle platooning is an important technology in modern transportation systems, offering significant improvements in highway traffic efficiency and fuel economy. Achieving coordinated behavior among vehicles in a platoon depends on wireless communication. However, packet losses in wireless communication can create critical safety issues when they occur together with sudden braking. In this paper, we propose a rigorous simulation-based method for studying such safety issues by analyzing the minimum inter-vehicle distance over time across control parameters that guarantee string stability. In particular, our method computes the exact distance at simulation time instants and guarantees that the change in distance between consecutive simulation time instants remains bounded. Therefore, the distances obtained at simulation times are representative of the continuous-time behavior, and the distances between those times can be accurately approximated. Our derivation relies on a lifted state representation and differential inequalities. For the proposed simulation method, we provide two approaches for selecting simulation times to ensure that the error in distance approximation remains within a given bound. We then extend our method to fuel-efficiency analysis, with guaranteed error bounds for calculating the average fuel savings of vehicles. Through an example involving a highway scenario with a merging lane, we demonstrate that among string-stable control parameter settings for a vehicle platoon, some perform better in terms of safety under simultaneous packet losses and sudden braking. We also identify control parameters that result in tradeoffs between safety and average fuel savings in a vehicle platoon.

papers.title: Classifier-Guided Latent Diffusion for Small-Molecule Generation
papers.summary: Diffusion models have emerged as a promising class of generative models for molecular design because of their ability to learn complex chemical distributions and support conditional or guided generation. In this work, we investigate a latent diffusion pipeline for property-guided small-molecule generation. The proposed framework represents canonicalized SMILES strings using a frozen ChemBERTa encoder, trains a Transformer-based decoder to reconstruct SELFIES strings from molecular latent embeddings, and learns an unconditional denoising diffusion model in the ChemBERTa latent space. To enable property-directed generation, a differentiable latent property predictor is used to guide the diffusion sampling process. Generated SELFIES strings are converted to SMILES, validated using RDKit, and evaluated using molecular validity, uniqueness, novelty, and predicted property scores. We study guidance toward two drug-relevant binary endpoints: blood--brain barrier permeability and inhibition of human $β$-secretase 1. The results suggest that latent diffusion over pretrained molecular embeddings can generate chemically valid and novel molecules while enabling controllable steering toward desired molecular properties.

papers.title: From Foundation VLM to Versatile Driving VLM: A Triplet Incremental Training Approach
papers.summary: Adapting general Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to Autonomous Driving (AD) is thought to require heavy 3D spatial priors or intrusive architectural overhauls to compensate for a lack of spatial grounding. In this work, we present a counterintuitive pilot study: off-the-shelf general VLMs already exhibit remarkable adaptability across diverse driving tasks, while precise metric depth remains the primary missing link, a bottleneck readily addressable via onboard sensors and depth foundation models. To this end, we introduce the Triplet Incremental Training Framework, a non-intrusive paradigm that seamlessly instills 3D geometric awareness into a general VLM backbone while fully preserving its open-world capabilities. Driven by automatically constructed (image, depth, QA pair) triplets, our framework operates via a unified tri-stream training pipeline: an unfrozen primary VLM stream to adapt to driving tasks, an auxiliary depth stream that guides the visual backbone to implicitly imagine 3D scene geometry via explicit geometric constraints, and a frozen twin VLM stream employing logit-level KL distillation to prevent semantic drift. Crucially, the auxiliary depth branch is discarded during deployment, ensuring the enhanced geometric awareness comes with zero inference overhead. We evaluate our framework across four major benchmarks targeting four diverse capabilities spanning 3D spatial perception, driving-oriented language reasoning, end-to-end planning, and general multimodal understanding. Our approach outperforms state-of-the-art driving VLMs, rivals domain-specific expert models in 3D perception, and successfully retains its original general reasoning capabilities. This demonstrates that Triplet Incremental Training offers a unified, deployment-ready paradigm for transforming general foundation models into robust driving intelligences.

papers.title: Achieving Robust Channel Estimation Neural Networks on Doppler effects by Designed Training Data
papers.summary: Channel estimation is crucial in wireless communication systems. Many existing works train and test their models using the same or similar channel. However, practical channels are infinitely diverse and time-variant while data-driven algorithms often degrade on new and previously unseen channels. This prohibits the practical implementation of neural networks for channel estimation, particularly in high speed scenarios characterized by rapidly channel profile changes and very high Doppler shifts. Online training can fine-tune models to adapt to new channels, but requires high computation resource and incurs significant latency for physical-layer devices. Moreover, online training cannot exhaustively cover all possible channels because there are infinitely many possible channels. Therefore, we investigate the ability of neural networks to generalize to wireless channels. This paper proposes design criteria to generate synthetic training data, which guaranty that the resulting networks perform robustly across wireless channels, especially for very high Doppler shifts and different Doppler spectra. It ensures that offline-trained neural networks require no prior information or online training to precisely estimate the new channels. To demonstrate general applicability, we use neural networks with different levels of complexity to show that the generalization achieved appears to be independent of architecture. From simulation results, neural networks achieve a certain performance across wireless channels with different unseen power delay profiles (PDP) and Doppler shifts.
